$comment: GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT. Source: tokens/units.json. Generator: scripts/build-tokens.mts (`pnpm run generate`). Gate: `pnpm check:generated`. This is the reviewable copy, with the authored policy attached; the copy that renders is the Unit/UNITS region inside lib/opsinjs.ts, because lib/generated/ does not travel with `shadcn add`. SAFETY: there is no reference range, threshold, plausibility bound, 'typical' value or default precision in this file, for any metric in any population. A unit table says what a number is measured in; it never says what a number should be. `generatedAt` carries the token source hash rather than a build time, because this file is guarded by a byte-for-byte drift gate.

policy.whyThisExists: A screen reader handed `mmHg` improvises a pronunciation, and the improvisation is rarely close. 'One twenty over eighty em em aitch gee' is a failure. The spoken form is the whole reason this table exists; the symbol is the part everybody remembers to supply.
policy.spoken: `spoken` is the wording for exactly one of the thing and `plural` is the wording for every other count, zero included. Both are British English, and that is a stated limit rather than a claim: a localised spoken form is not in this table yet, so a component asked for a non-English locale gets English words beside locale-formatted digits. Naming the gap is the honest state; inventing translations is not.
policy.precision: THERE IS NO DEFAULT PRECISION IN THIS FILE, and its absence is the point. health/numbers-units-precision is canonical and its rule 2 reads 'Precision is a property of the metric, not of the value'. A unit is not a metric: blood glucose and cholesterol are both reported in mmol/L and do not share a number of decimal places, and a per-unit default would therefore be wrong for one of them on every screen. Decimal places travel with the measurement, from the product, or they are not asserted at all.
policy.conversion: A conversion belongs here only when it is a mathematical fact — an exact definition of one unit in terms of another. Every one carries `basis`, which names the definition it comes from. `toBase` is how to reach the family's base unit; the generator composes the full pairwise closure from it, in exact integer arithmetic, in both directions. A unit with no `toBase` converts to nothing, and that renders as an explicit 'we do not have this' rather than a substituted default.
policy.refusal: `refusedConversions` is the load-bearing half. A pair listed there is one that people expect to be arithmetic and is not, and each row says why. Publishing a factor for one of them would invite somebody to apply the glucose factor to cholesterol — see health/unit-systems, which states the non-goal directly: 'opsinjs ships no factors and no thresholds. Your clinical source owns the factor; the interface owns the labelling.'
policy.lookup: Units are found by their exact `symbol`, case included. There is no fuzzy matching and no alias list, because a table that guesses which unit somebody meant is a table that will one day guess wrong about a concentration. An unrecognised symbol resolves to nothing, and the component renders the symbol as written rather than guessing at a pronunciation.

units.basis: The base unit of this family.

The Fahrenheit scale is defined against Celsius: a Fahrenheit degree is exactly five ninths of a Celsius degree and the scales meet where 32 °F is 0 °C, so °C = °F × 5/9 − 160/9. This conversion is affine rather than a ratio, which is why a temperature and a temperature DIFFERENCE do not convert the same way — 2 °C of change is 3.6 °F of change, not 35.6 °F.
The SI prefix 'kilo' is exactly one thousand. This is a definition of the prefix, not a measurement of anything.
The base unit of this family. Every other mass in this table is defined against it.

The international avoirdupois pound is defined as exactly 0.45359237 kilograms by the 1959 international yard and pound agreement. An exact definition, adopted by every signatory, and not a rounded measurement.

One stone is exactly fourteen avoirdupois pounds, and one pound is exactly 0.45359237 kilograms; fourteen times that is 6.35029318 kilograms exactly. Two definitions composed, no measurement involved. Note the plural: British body weight is 'eleven stone', not 'eleven stones'.

refusedConversions.reason: There is more than one calorie. The thermochemical calorie is exactly 4.184 joules and the fifteen-degree calorie is not, and food energy labelling picks one by regulation rather than by physics. Naming a single factor here would hide which calorie was meant, so the pair is refused until this file can carry the choice explicitly.

Molar concentration and mass concentration are related by the molar mass of the substance being measured, which is a property of the SUBSTANCE and not of either unit. Glucose, cholesterol and creatinine each carry a different factor, and this table does not know which analyte a reading is. A single published factor here would be applied to all three by somebody in a hurry, and the answer would be wrong by a multiple rather than by a rounding.

The two ways of reporting HbA1c are related by a fitted regression between two assay standardisations, not by an exact definition. A regression is a measurement with a residual, it is periodically re-fitted, and it belongs to the laboratory that reports the result. This table carries definitions only.
